title: Used Fable 5 - After about 7 Claude iterations (switching to opus) here is what it spit out
author: The-Doodle-Dude
selftext:
Here is the first prompt I used. I’ve reiterated about 7 prompts since then

\# UPDATED GAME DIRECTION

Revise the game from a 2D pixel art tower defense game into a \*\*3D survival tower defense / exploration / base-building game\*\*.

The game is now:

\* 3D

\* Third-person or isometric camera

\* Exploration-based

\* Base-building focused

\* Wave survival focused

\* Modern UI

\* Multiple enemy waves

\* Multiple building types

\* Multiple building upgrades

\---

\# UPDATED GAME CONCEPT

\*\*Dwarf Defense\*\* is a \*\*3D survival tower defense and base-building game\*\* where the player controls a dwarf explorer in a dangerous prehistoric fantasy world.

The player starts alone on the map, explores the environment, gathers resources, chooses where to establish a base, then builds defenses to survive escalating dinosaur waves.

The game should feel like a hybrid of:

\* Warcraft 3 custom maps

\* Valheim-style exploration and base building

\* Orcs Must Die-style defense planning

\* Kingdom Rush-style tower progression

\* They Are Billions-style wave survival

\---

\# VISUAL STYLE

The game should use a stylized 3D fantasy look.

Avoid:

\* hyper-realism

\* mobile-game cartoon look

\* overly cute assets

Preferred style:

\* stylized low-poly or mid-poly 3D

\* dwarven fantasy architecture

\* rugged wilderness

\* readable dinosaurs

\* strong silhouettes

\* modern clean UI

\* polished PC game presentation

Environment themes:

\* rocky plains

\* pine forests

\* caves

\* volcanic regions

\* ancient ruins

\* river valleys

\* mountain passes

\---

\# CAMERA REQUIREMENTS

Recommend the best camera style for this game.

Preferred options:

\* isometric / angled RTS camera

\* third-person exploration camera

\* hybrid camera where player explores in third-person but defense mode zooms out

Choose one recommended camera style and justify it.

The camera must support:

\* exploration

\* base planning

\* building placement

\* combat visibility

\* wave defense readability

\---

\# CORE GAMEPLAY LOOP

The full gameplay loop must be:

1. Player spawns as a dwarf on a 3D map

2. Player explores the map

3. Player gathers starter resources

4. Player scouts defensible terrain

5. Player places a Town Hall / Base Core

6. The base becomes the enemy target

7. Player builds defensive structures

8. Wave 1 begins

9. Player survives and earns resources

10. Player upgrades buildings

11. Player expands base

12. Stronger waves arrive

13. New dinosaur enemy types appear

14. Player unlocks advanced towers and walls

15. Boss waves occur at major milestones

\---

\# WAVE SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

The game must include a robust multi-wave system.

Minimum wave requirements:

\* At least 10 waves for MVP vertical slice

\* Increasing enemy count per wave

\* Increasing enemy strength per wave

\* New enemy types introduced over time

\* Boss or elite wave every 5 waves

\* Downtime between waves

\* UI countdown before next wave

\* Option to start next wave early for bonus resources

Wave examples:

Wave 1:

Small raptors only

Wave 2:

More raptors

Wave 3:

Raptors and armored young triceratops

Wave 4:

Fast pack raptors

Wave 5:

Mini-boss dinosaur

Wave 6:

Mixed enemies

Wave 7:

Ranged spitters introduced

Wave 8:

Tank dinosaurs introduced

Wave 9:

Large swarm wave

Wave 10:

Boss wave

\---

\# BUILDING SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

The game must include multiple building types.

Core buildings:

\## Town Hall / Base Core

Main base structure.

If destroyed:

Game Over.

Upgradeable.

Upgrade effects:

\* increases base health

\* unlocks building tiers

\* increases resource storage

\* unlocks advanced tech

\## Arrow Tower

Basic tower.

Upgrade path:

\* Tier 1: Wooden Arrow Tower

\* Tier 2: Reinforced Archer Tower

\* Tier 3: Ballista Tower

\## Cannon Tower

Area damage tower.

Upgrade path:

\* Tier 1: Stone Cannon

\* Tier 2: Iron Cannon

\* Tier 3: Explosive Mortar

\## Rune Tower

Magic tower.

Upgrade path:

\* Tier 1: Rune Spark Tower

\* Tier 2: Arcane Rune Tower

\* Tier 3: Storm Obelisk

\## Wall

Blocks or slows enemy movement.

Upgrade path:

\* Tier 1: Wood Wall

\* Tier 2: Stone Wall

\* Tier 3: Iron-Reinforced Wall

\## Resource Hut

Improves resource income.

Upgrade path:

\* Tier 1: Gatherer Hut

\* Tier 2: Mining Depot

\* Tier 3: Dwarven Resource Guild

\## Workshop

Unlocks upgrades.

Upgrade path:

\* Tier 1: Basic Workshop

\* Tier 2: Engineering Workshop

\* Tier 3: Master Forge

\---

\# BUILDING UPGRADE REQUIREMENTS

Every major defensive building should support upgrades.

Upgrade system must include:

\* upgrade cost

\* upgrade time or instant upgrade decision

\* improved stats

\* visual change per tier

\* UI button for upgrade

\* locked tiers until requirements are met

Building stats to support:

\* health

\* damage

\* range

\* fire rate

\* armor

\* splash radius

\* special effect

\* upgrade tier

Upgrade examples:

Arrow Tower:

Tier 1:

Damage 10

Range 12

Fire Rate 1.0

Tier 2:

Damage 18

Range 14

Fire Rate 0.85

Tier 3:

Damage 32

Range 16

Fire Rate 0.7

Special: armor piercing

Cannon Tower:

Tier 1:

Damage 25

Splash 3

Tier 2:

Damage 45

Splash 4

Tier 3:

Damage 75

Splash 5

Special: knockback

Rune Tower:

Tier 1:

Damage 15

Tier 2:

Damage 30

Special: slow

Tier 3:

Damage 55

Special: chain lightning

\---

\# ENEMY REQUIREMENTS

Enemies must be 3D dinosaurs with distinct roles.

Enemy types:

\## Raptor

Fast weak swarm enemy.

\## Armored Raptor

Medium health, slightly armored.

\## Triceratops

Slow tank enemy.

\## Spitter

Ranged enemy that attacks towers.

\## Ankylosaurus

Heavy armor siege enemy.

\## Pterodactyl

Flying enemy that ignores walls.

\## T-Rex Boss

Major boss enemy.

Enemy stats:

\* health

\* speed

\* damage

\* armor

\* attack range

\* target preference

\* reward value

\* wave tier

Enemy behavior:

\* path toward Town Hall

\* attack buildings in path

\* prioritize base if path is open

\* some enemies target towers

\* flying enemies ignore walls

\* boss enemies damage multiple structures

\---

\# RESOURCE SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

Resources:

\## Gold

Used for:

\* towers

\* upgrades

\* repairs

Earned from:

\* killing enemies

\* wave completion

\* exploration rewards

\## Wood

Used for:

\* early buildings

\* walls

\* basic towers

Gathered from:

\* trees

\* resource nodes

\## Stone

Used for:

\* advanced towers

\* walls

\* Town Hall upgrades

Gathered from:

\* rock nodes

\## Ore

Used for:

\* high-tier upgrades

\* mechanical towers

\* workshop upgrades

Gathered from:

\* ore deposits

\---

\# MODERN UI REQUIREMENTS

Replace the old pixel-art UI direction with a \*\*modern 3D strategy UI\*\*.

UI style:

\* clean

\* dark translucent panels

\* bronze/gold accents

\* subtle rune highlights

\* modern PC strategy game layout

\* readable typography

\* responsive scaling

\* no mobile-game bubble buttons

Required UI elements:

\## Top Resource Bar

Displays:

\* gold

\* wood

\* stone

\* ore

\* current wave

\* time until next wave

\## Bottom Build Bar

Displays:

\* buildable structures

\* hotkeys

\* costs

\* locked/unlocked state

\## Selected Building Panel

When a building is selected, show:

\* name

\* health

\* tier

\* damage

\* range

\* upgrade button

\* repair button

\* sell button

\## Wave Alert UI

Displays:

\* incoming wave countdown

\* enemy types in next wave

\* boss wave warning

\## Upgrade UI

Shows:

\* current tier

\* next tier

\* cost

\* stat improvements

\* requirements

\## Game Over UI

Shows:

\* wave survived

\* enemies killed

\* base status

\* restart button

\---

\# 3D BUILD PLACEMENT REQUIREMENTS

The game must support 3D building placement.

Required behavior:

\* player selects building from UI

\* ghost preview appears on terrain

\* preview follows mouse cursor/raycast

\* green preview if valid

\* red preview if invalid

\* building cannot overlap another building

\* building cannot be placed on steep terrain

\* building cannot be placed too close to enemy spawn

\* building snaps to optional grid if enabled

\* click confirms placement

\* right-click cancels placement

\---

\# IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENTS

Claude must produce:

1. Final 3D game design document

2. Technical architecture

3. Engine recommendation

4. Scene hierarchy

5. Script architecture

6. Full implementation roadmap

7. Building system implementation

8. Upgrade system implementation

9. Wave system implementation

10. 3D placement system implementation

11. Modern UI implementation

12. Enemy AI implementation

13. Resource system implementation

14. Save/load design

15. Vertical slice plan

Claude must provide full scripts whenever code is needed.

Claude must use one recommended implementation path and avoid overwhelming me with alternatives.

Claude must debug one issue at a time.

\---

\# FIRST IMPLEMENTATION TARGET

The first vertical slice should include:

\* 3D player movement

\* explorable terrain

\* Town Hall placement

\* 3 buildable towers

\* 3 enemy types

\* 10 waves

\* gold/wood/stone resources

\* tower upgrades to Tier 3

\* modern UI resource bar

\* building selection panel

\* wave countdown UI

\* game over condition

replies.body: What's your process for this?

replies.author: PlaidWorld
replies.body: I asked Claude if I give you the data from fall out 3 can you make a model viewer using GODOT and it just grew from there. Anyhow you can try that and it should make a basic model viewer in like 20 minutes. After that its weeks of black magic to get rendering correct... Mind you I was a lead programmer on ESO that that helps. You really do have to guide the AI to make the correct things and optimize etc.

replies.author: PlaidWorld
replies.body: The process is slow and non trivial weeks of grinding away at bugs mostly. Rendering is the hard part. The AI actually did a pretty great job of reverse engineering the scripting engine used. Now that rendering is work Im slowly implementing more and more of the game play.

replies.author: GoodguyGastly
replies.body: I'm curious why you'd want to do this? Like is there a greater goal or just to see if you could?

replies.author: PlaidWorld
replies.body: Well when I worked for ZOS they would never let me port these games to Mac. So theres that... Now I can in some weeks while still working on other things. I learned a lot about the engine doing it. What to do with it? Maybe open source it. Makes a neat GODOT tech demo. Maybe use it as the base for my own Bethesda style games. I really have not decided yet. I have 6 games in production now. Anything I make using this comes after all that. Anyhow thats the ideas I have had so far.

replies.author: GoodguyGastly
replies.body: I love the idea of using it for your own Bethesda games. My current game (shown on profile) is inspired by them too, to some extent, but I struggle with level design and environments. I've always thought it would be nice to have my favorite locations from those games as a base and to just remix it.
